name: Development of Medieval Siege Technology
summary: The counterweight trebuchet, developed in the 12th century, transforms medieval siege warfare, capable of hurling 100-300 kg projectiles with devastating accuracy, it makes most older castle designs vulnerable. The Crusader states' concentrated castle-building (Krak des Chevaliers, Margat) responds to this threat with concentric defenses, round towers, and more complex approaches. Artillery specialists (engineers) become crucial military figures.

_quarry.structural_significance: The trebuchet-castle arms race drives one of the great medieval engineering developments; Krak des Chevaliers (built 1142-1271) represents the peak of medieval defensive architecture in response to trebuchet threat; the same arms race produces the German Ordensburgen of the Teutonic Knights and Edward I's Welsh castles; the eventual superiority of gunpowder artillery (after 1380) over the trebuchet marks the end of the castle as a reliable defensive solution
